summary: B is the more reviewable, narrowly scoped patch, although it still needs correction before merge. A introduces a prohibited global retry/body-lifecycle refactor and duplicates Files.Add’s request logic.
reasons: B reuses multipartbody.NewFile, implements the exact Upload signature, validates inputs, and keeps request option/response handling centralized in a shared service helper.
A’s Upload directly duplicates FilesService.Add’s request construction, decoding, and error handling instead of routing through Add, creating maintenance drift.

A modifies RawClient body replay and ownership semantics across the SDK, despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated retry refactoring. Its shared io.ReadSeeker rewinding also broadens behavioral and concurrency risk.
B’s changes are confined to FilesService and its tests, making the remaining contract violations substantially easier to fix and review.
risks_a: Upload does not call FilesService.Add and duplicates its implementation.
The RawClient change alters behavior for all seekable request bodies, including content-length calculation, closing behavior, and retries.

FilesService.Add behavior changes indirectly for seekable bodies, conflicting with the requirement to preserve it unchanged beyond the new convenience path and update its comment accordingly introduces behavior claims outside scope and changelog/README amplify the unsupported contract expansion beyond scope.. It also adds broad documentation and tests for behavior outside the requested scope. A lacks a source-reader failure test.
risks_b: Upload calls a new private add helper rather than the required existing FilesService.Add method.
Add now eagerly reads and buffers every caller-provided body, changing its established streaming, memory, and error-timing behavior in violation of the frozen contract.
Tests omit explicit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader failure coverage.
